title: Altering signal sensitivity without changing the model predicts specific birth defects

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Altering signal sensitivity without changing the model predicts specific birth defects

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the active-inference morphogenesis model, changing cells' sensitivity to extracellular, exogenous or intracellular signals without changing the generative model produces specific dysmorphogenesis, e.g. reducing sensitivity to the head-expressed signal shrinks the head, and doubling sensitivity to intracellular signals causes failed migration, differentiation and atrophy; these are predictions for pharmacological manipulation of intercellular signalling.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: More selective interventions produce a dysmorphogenesis of various segments of the target morphology: reducing sensitivity to the second chemotactic signal—that is expressed by head cells—reduces the size of the head.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Simulating regeneration and dysmorphogenesis”. Scope: Active-inference morphogenesis simulation; proposed for real embryos under signalling perturbation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The in-silico portion is directly reproducible, but the claim explicitly presents the outputs as predictions for real embryos. Existing materials resolve the model behavior, not the biological generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run each sensitivity perturbation and measure segment sizes, migration, differentiation, and atrophy relative to baseline. The simulation predictions are confirmed by the specified phenotypes, but validating them in embryos would require matching public perturbation-and-anatomy data.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Model signal sensitivities do not map uniquely to biological targets.

The in vivo pharmacological prediction lacks a matched public dataset.

operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The in-model half can be probed by editing precisions in the public solver, although the exact 2015 sensitivity settings have to be reconstructed from the paper. The further claim that the same manipulations are predictions for pharmacological treatment of real embryos has no matching public perturbation series, so only the simulation half is testable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the public model, lower the precision or gain on the head-associated chemotactic signal and, separately, raise intracellular-signal precision, then measure segment size, migration, and differentiation. The in-model phenotypes can be confirmed or refuted that way; the pharmacological reading for real embryos needs embryo cohorts that pair those signal changes with anatomy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public embryo dataset maps this model's signal channels onto a drug and an anatomical readout.

The head-shrinking and failed-migration cases are described in prose, not as named switches in the current script.
